about: The one machine-readable home of the krish-voice kill list and the per-channel scored checks. Control Center's voice check (api/_voiceCheck.ts, the check_voice connector tool and the engines' voice-check route) reads this file live from main. Hard rules hold a draft for rewrite; scored rules only advise. Prose rules live in voice-doctrine.md, voice-profile.md and linkedin-evidence.md; this file must agree with them (evals/voice/test-kill-list.mjs checks it). Characters that other guards scan for are written as \u escapes.
rulings: Ruling (Krish, 2026-11-07): British spelling everywhere, including krishraja.com.
Ruling (Krish, 2026-11-07): a hard fail holds the draft for one rewrite; style is scored with fixes beside every draft.
Ruling (Krish, 2026-11-07, superseded 2026-11-09 by the ruling below): the voice system covers emails from his box, Jonny's emails in his style, his personal LinkedIn and his other personal socials.
Ruling (Krish, 2026-11-09): every word written for Krish, Jonny or the publication passes the one voice check.

comment.max_chars_source: LinkedIn's comment box limit (1,250 characters), the same platform limit as its other channel limits.

clip.about: A product clip's spoken script and title (Growth > clips), in the product's own voice under krish-voice's rules; never the publication's canon, whose product_in_editorial veto (at the pinned hash) refuses a product name in an editorial piece.

exempt.about: Matches inside these strings never count. Proper names and fixed framework labels only.

em_dash.message: No em dashes. Use a comma, a full stop or brackets.

words.source: voice-doctrine.md, Words and phrases to avoid, and Canon banned language
words.message: "{match}" is on the kill list. Name the mechanism, number or decision it hides.

list: at the end of the day
i hope this message finds you
i hope this email finds you

us_spellings.about: US spellings that have a British form. Whole words, case-insensitive. Krish ruled British spelling everywhere on 2026-11-07.

engagement_bait.about: LinkedIn demotes it (linkedin-evidence.md rule 4, primary) and it pushes rather than invites (voice-profile ruling 2). Patterns run case-sensitive with the u flag; case is spelled out in each pattern.
engagement_bait.message: Engagement bait. Invite a real answer instead.

unicode_bold.about: Mathematical alphanumeric symbols used as fake bold or italic. Retired by voice-profile ruling 3.

emoji_bullets.about: A line that starts with an emoji used as a bullet. Retired by voice-profile ruling 3.
emoji_bullets.message: No emoji bullets. One emoji for feeling, on LinkedIn only.

self_name.about: The personal accounts growth-makeyourmindup drafts for (X, Threads, Substack Notes, Instagram) never name him (its ACCOUNT-VOICE.md, Krish 2026-10-28: "Remember, no content refers to Krish, ever."). His own LinkedIn is first person and is not covered; emails may sign or mention him.
self_name.message: A personal post never names Krish.

emoji_count.about: At most one emoji, for feeling, on LinkedIn; none in emails (voice-profile ruling 3).
emoji_count.message: Too many emoji: {count}. At most {max} here.

context_words.about: Banned as metaphor only, so a human or the rewrite judges them.
context_words.message: "{match}" is banned as a metaphor. Keep it only if it is literal.

list: thank you so much for taking
pronoun_openers.message: Drop the subject pronoun or generic opener. Start at the point.

patterns: ^(in summary|in conclusion|to sum up|to conclude|overall,|in short,)
summary_endings.message: End on a verdict, not a summary.

patterns: \b(i hope|let me know what you think|let me know your thoughts|thoughts\?)[^.!?]*[.!?]?\s*$
soft_closers.message: No soft closer. Land a verdict or one specific next step.

first_line_length.fix: Make the first line a complete claim in about 110 characters.

first_line_concrete.fix: Open on a number, something you did or saw, or a defensible claim.

patterns: ^(in|as|with|recently|lately|today|this week|over the past|i wanted|i've been|i have been|so,|here's|let's|we all know|everyone)\b
no_setup_opener.fix: Cut the setup. Start where the point starts.

length_band.fix: One sharp idea under about 150 words, or a full argument of about 900 to 1,500 characters.

blank_line_ratio.fix: Join the one-line paragraphs. It reads as broetry.

hashtags.fix: Drop the hashtags; three at most.

closing_question.fix: One specific, easy-to-answer question at most, and never "Thoughts?".

email_length.fix: Cold notes land at about 50 to 100 words. Cut what repeats.

subject_words.fix: A subject of one to four words, like a note from a person.

questions.fix: One question at most, and one ask.

score.about: distance from 0 (reads like Krish and passes every scored check) to 1. It combines the fingerprint distance (evals/voice/fingerprint.mjs, his register) with the share of scored checks that fail. A signal, never a verdict (voice-profile.md).

voices.about: Who speaks on a channel. krish and jonny take krish-voice's rules; publication takes them too and adds Make Your Mind Up's own canon, which its repository owns and this file admits only at the reviewed hash below.
